shortlist: Hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein tumor thrombus

selector.rationale: The patient has a history of colon cancer and the liver lesion has characteristics consistent with metastasis, such as a solid portion that enhances in the early phase and washes out in the delayed phase.

rejected.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein tumor thrombus
rejected.why: The patient's hepatitis B and C serologies were negative, reducing the likelihood of hepatocellular carcinoma.

rejected.label: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: Bile cytology was negative for malignancy, making intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma less likely.

rejected.label: Colorectal cancer metastasis
rejected.why: This is a less specific diagnosis compared to liver metastasis from colon cancer, given the patient's history of colon cancer.

support_spans: A 55-year-old man underwent right hemicolectomy for moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon
Thirteen months after surgery, follow-up CT revealed a 25 mm lesion in segment 8 of the liver
CTA demonstrated a liver tumor with two components: a solid portion that enhanced in the early phase and washed out in the delayed phase, and a cystic component
